scenario: A wildfire is approaching a hospital and an eastern residential district. Twenty patients cannot be moved without buses. Three hundred eastern residents need those same buses to evacuate. Fifty firefighters are on scene. The coordinator must choose one plan. The buses cannot be divided, no reinforcements will arrive, and delay is not an option. Plan A sends the buses to the hospital. The patients' escape is then almost certain. The eastern district must use a narrow road with a 10% chance of blockage. If the road is blocked, about sixty residents could be trapped. Using the buses for the hospital does not increase that blockage risk. Plan B sends the buses east. Nearly all 300 residents then escape safely. The patients remain. Fire-resistant walls make their deaths unlikely. There is a 20% chance the hospital ventilation system fails. If it does, patients who cannot be moved face near-certain death. Five firefighters stay to assist them at moderate risk. Which plan should the coordinator choose?

Twenty patients cannot be moved without buses.
Three hundred eastern residents need those same buses to evacuate.
The coordinator must choose one plan.

Plan A sends the buses to the hospital.
The patients' escape is then almost certain.

If the road is blocked, about sixty residents could be trapped.
Using the buses for the hospital does not increase that blockage risk.
Plan B sends the buses east.
Nearly all 300 residents then escape safely.
Fire-resistant walls make their deaths unlikely.

If it does, patients who cannot be moved face near-certain death.
Five firefighters stay to assist them at moderate risk.
